audit.description: Changed production code imports and calls the real target library: `vyper/remote.py` replaces `import toml` with `import tomli` and returns `tomli.loads`, and `vyper/util.py` replaces `import toml` with `import tomli` and parses TOML via `tomli.loads`. Static and dynamic evidence show no source-library imports from production repo code, while dynamic target events originate from installed `site-packages/tomli` rather than a local provider.
evidence: Unified diff: `vyper/remote.py` changes `import toml` to `import tomli` and `toml.loads` to `tomli.loads`.
Unified diff: `vyper/util.py` changes `import toml` to `import tomli` and updates TOML parsing paths to call `tomli.loads`.
Static anti-cheat: `vyper/remote.py` and `vyper/util.py` have `imports_target: true`, `imports_source: false`, and `fake_target_added_code: false`.
Dynamic anti-cheat: target imports observed from production repo files `vyper/remote.py` and `vyper/util.py`, with origin under `site-packages/tomli`.
reasons: Production files meaningfully use tomli, not just dependency metadata.
No changed production file imports or dynamically uses toml in the provided static evidence.
Dynamic evidence reports target imports from production files and zero source imports from production repo code.
No fake local tomli provider was detected; target origin is installed site-packages.
